title: Internal semisimplicial types in ordinary HoTT
formal: In the fixed ordinary HoTT theory T below, can one define a single internal family \(S:\mathbb{N} \to U_{1}\) and restriction maps \(r_{n}:S(n+1)\to S(n)\) whose finite stages are equivalent, compatibly with restriction, to the canonical finite semisimplicial telescopes \(D_{n}\)?
definitions: Fix T to be intensional Martin–Löf type theory with dependent function and pair types \(\Pi ,\Sigma\), identity types with their J eliminator, empty and unit types, finite coproducts, natural numbers and W-types, a cumulative predicative sequence \(U_{0}:U_{1}:\cdots\) closed under these constructors, and univalence for these universes. Also allow propositional truncation and homotopy pushouts with their ordinary dependent eliminators and propositional computation rules for path constructors, as in the HoTT book. There is no equality reflection, axiom K/UIP, resizing, choice, excluded middle, second equality type, display modality, or additional primitive for semisimplicial types. The question concerns definability in this specified theory; a negative result would apply to this theory, not automatically to every possible extension called HoTT. Define an external, finite family of syntactic telescopes as follows. \(D_{0}\) is \(U_{0}\), with element \(A_{0}\). Given data \(d=(A_{0},\ldots ,A_{j- 1})\) in \(D_{j- 1}\), form \(B_{j}(d)\), the dependent type of labelled boundaries of a j-simplex: for every nonempty proper subset F of \(\{0,\ldots ,j\}\), in increasing cardinality and then lexicographic order, choose a label \(x_{F}\) in \(A_{|F|- 1}\) evaluated on the labels of all nonempty proper subfaces of F. Identify F with \(\{0,\ldots ,|F|- 1\}\) by its increasing enumeration when supplying these arguments. For singleton F this means \(x_{F}:A_{0}\). Set \(D_{j}=\Sigma (d:D_{j- 1})(B_{j}(d)\to U_{0})\), whose last field is \(A_{j}\), and let \(p_{j}:D_{j+1}\to D_{j}\) forget the last field. This describes an ordinary finite T-expression for each external integer j; it does not postulate an internal function \(j\mapsto D_{j}\). The required output is finite closed T-terms \(S:\mathbb{N} \to U_{1}\) and \(r:\Pi (n:\mathbb{N} )(S(n+1)\to S(n))\), together with a metatheoretic proof that for every external j there are T-terms \(e_{j}:S(j)\)≃\(D_{j}\) and homotopies \(e_{j}\circ r_{j} \sim  p_{j}\circ e_{j+1}\). Here j inside T denotes its numeral, ≃ is the usual type equivalence, and ~ is pointwise identity. No judgmental equality between \(S(j)\) and \(D_{j}\) is required. The equivalences classify the full type-valued telescopes, with arbitrary \(U_{0}\)-small simplex types and no fixed truncation bound.
answer_criterion: Prove that the specified theory T admits finite closed terms S and r together with the external stagewise equivalences and compatibility homotopies required above, or prove that no such terms and witnesses exist in T. The positive conclusion must hold at every external finite stage and allow arbitrary \(U_{0}\)-small simplex types.
why: Determine whether ordinary HoTT can express a fundamental unbounded coherent structure internally, a basic issue for higher categories and foundational proof languages.

importance.reason: A central expressiveness problem for homotopy type theory; precise internal construction would remove a major obstacle to formalizing higher structures without enriching the theory.

progress.text: The HoTT book supplies the ordinary dependent-type, univalence and higher-inductive framework fixed for this card.
Kraus states the uniform finite-level semisimplicial family problem and explains its connection to higher categories and internal metatheory.
Annenkov and coauthors develop the two-level framework and distinguish outer-indexed constructions from inner semisimplicial universes.
Chen’s thesis develops internal-model methods but explicitly marks the classifier construction incomplete and the unrestricted ordinary-HoTT problem open.
The journal version of Displayed Type Theory gives semisimplicial types using additional modal/display primitives; the preprint dates from 2023–2024.
Two-Level Type Theory v5 updates typos and references while retaining the distinction between ordinary HoTT and enriched constructions.

context_blocks.text: Homotopy type theory treats identity as mathematical data that can itself have nontrivial identities. This makes it a natural setting for spaces and higher structures, but it changes what it means to give a diagram. In set-level mathematics, equations between composites can be recorded once and used without further information. For general types, chosen identifications can have multiple distinct witnesses, and comparisons between those witnesses may matter in the next dimension.

A semisimplicial type begins with a type \(A_{0}\) of vertices. For every ordered pair of vertices, \(A_{1}\) gives a type of edges. For every triangle boundary—three vertices and three specified edges—\(A_{2}\) gives a type of fillers. At dimension three, a filler is indexed by four vertices, six edges and four triangular fillers sharing their appropriate faces. Nothing forces a filler to exist, and the type of fillers may itself have arbitrarily rich homotopy.

The finite telescope description records shared boundaries through dependent types. A triangle’s three edges are already assigned the required endpoints; one does not choose unrelated edges and then append a collection of endpoint equations. The same idea works at each externally fixed dimension. The difficulty is making the whole construction into one function that accepts an internal natural number, rather than a growing list of separately written definitions.

This is why the card distinguishes its externally specified \(D_{j}\) from the sought internal S. A script can generate the expression for \(D_{100}\) and a type checker can check it. That does not supply a HoTT term whose argument is an arbitrary \(n:\mathbb{N}\). The compatibility requirement also matters: a collection of unrelated types with the right apparent sizes would not tell us how to forget the highest-dimensional data.

The statement deliberately allows equivalence at each stage instead of demanding a particular syntactic normal form. Thus a clever alternative encoding can solve the problem if it represents all the prescribed data and respects truncation. Once the internal tower exists, dependent sums, products and identity types already express a compatible infinite sequence. The missing step is constructing the tower itself, not adding a primitive that merely asserts an infinite sequence exists.

Kraus’s TYPES 2018 discussion identifies uniform finite-dimensional semisimplicial types as a major open problem and explains their role in higher category theory. Adding suitable Segal and completeness conditions to such data provides a route toward internal higher categories. Those conditions are additional structure: this card asks first for unrestricted semisimplicial data, with no composition, identity or horn-filling axioms imposed.

Two-level type theory introduces an outer equality satisfying uniqueness of identity proofs, alongside the homotopical inner theory. It can formalize constructions indexed by outer natural numbers. Annenkov, Capriotti, Kraus and Sattler distinguish this from constructing an inner universe of infinite semisimplicial types; additional hypotheses relating the two natural-number objects support the latter. The May 2026 revision is labelled a typo and reference update, not a new solution in ordinary HoTT.

Displayed Type Theory takes another route. Kolomatskaia and Shulman introduce discrete and simplicial modes together with a primitive display operation, then use it for a coinductive construction of semisimplicial types. This is a substantive solution in their enriched system, with a detailed semantic correctness argument. It does not give a definition from the constructors of T alone, because those additional primitives are precisely what enable the construction.

Chen’s 2025 thesis studies internal models and Reedy-fibrant inverse diagrams directly. It explicitly retains the ordinary-HoTT semisimplicial problem as open. Section 6.1 labels its proposed classifier construction a sketch whose Agda formalization has unresolved termination and definitional-equality issues, and states that it is not intended to solve the unrestricted problem. This is useful progress toward articulating the required coherence, rather than a completed internal classifier.

A set-valued construction also does not suffice. If every simplex type is a set, identities between elements have no higher ambiguity, and ordinary categorical equations behave much more rigidly. The requirement that the simplex types range over \(U_{0}\) preserves the higher-dimensional content that motivates the problem. Likewise, having a satisfactory semantic construction in a model does not automatically produce a finite term definable in the specified syntax.

A positive answer would show that ordinary dependent types can organize this fundamental form of unbounded coherence without additional structure in the language. A negative answer would identify a precise expressive limitation and help explain why successful alternative foundations introduce new primitives. Either outcome would guide the design of proof assistants intended to support higher category theory and internal constructions of type-theoretic models.

sentences: Semisimplicial types organize vertices, edges, triangles and higher-dimensional fillers with compatible shared boundaries.
Ordinary homotopy type theory can describe any fixed finite collection of these stages externally.
The project asks for one internal family indexed by natural numbers, together with compatible maps forgetting the highest stage.
Higher identities carry data, so specifying all coherence requirements uniformly is harder than listing equations in ordinary set-based mathematics.
Such a construction would provide an internal foundation for important higher-dimensional structures without extending the stated type theory.
